stem: Which presentation best matches the defining pattern of a major depressive episode?

options.A: At least 2 weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest/pleasure with additional depressive symptoms
options.B: One day of sadness that resolves without functional change
options.C: At least 7 days of elevated mood, increased energy, and decreased need for sleep
options.D: Fear restricted to a single object with no depressive symptoms

rationale: NIMH describes a major depressive episode as a period of at least 2 weeks with depressed mood or loss of interest or pleasure plus a majority of specified symptoms such as sleep, eating, energy, concentration, or self-worth problems.
educational_objective: Recognize the minimum duration and core mood/anhedonia pattern of a major depressive episode.
source_claim_supported: A major depressive episode includes at least 2 weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest/pleasure with additional specified depressive symptoms.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 / PDF p.14
correction_summary: Added the required 2-week duration and removed vague symptom-only wording.
audit_findings: A uniquely matches the NIMH definition. B is too brief; C is a manic pattern; D is a phobic pattern. No second answer remains.
audit_reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol Rule 1 — final semantic audit
